subject: Post-demo action: prioritized model slate + regression guardrails
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Khan <sara@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo action: prioritized model slate + regression guardrails

Hi Sara — thanks again for today’s demo call. Quick recap and recommended next steps so your team can align with engineering: 

TL;DR: Recommended shortlist (prioritized) for the PoC: 1) RedOpt-13B-8q (balanced latency/cost, strong on safety), 2) Falcon-40B-INT8-light (higher quality on long-form, higher cost), 3) Llama2-70B-quantized (fallback for edge-case accuracy). Rationale below.

Why this slate: 
- RedOpt-13B-8q: median latency ~120ms p50 (our hosted measurements for 256-token bursts), best sweet spot for your interactive UI targets and under your cost ceiling.
- Falcon-40B-INT8-light: higher pass@1 for the long-tail content in your sample set (legal/terms), but ~2–3x cost vs. RedOpt. Strong fallback when confidence < 0.6.
- Llama2-70B-quantized: use only for select evaluation slices (complex multi-step reasoning) where recall matters more than latency.

Quality/regression concerns: we saw a small drop (~4–6% accuracy) on the contract-extraction benchmark when moving from full-fp32 to 8-bit variants for two prompt templates in your pack. We recommend a guarded rollout: enable 8-bit by default but gate the two sensitive prompt sets behind thresholding + sampling-based quality checks.

Action items / next steps: 
1) Your team: confirm which evaluation slices we should prioritize (legal clauses, billing flow, customer support transcripts) — Rajesh suggested legal & billing first.
2) Redwood: deliver a prioritized prompt set (attached) + benchmark link and a short eval run showing per-slice deltas by model/quant config (attached).
3) Schedule a 30m alignment with your infra + security folks to confirm VPC/network requirements for the Dedicated trial (Rajesh/Procurement).

Attachments: nimbus_prompt_set_v1.txt (sample prompts & templates), latency_cost_estimates.csv (cost projection for 10k sessions/day), eval-runs-20261210.zip (summary html inside linked above).

If this captures it, I’ll send a short canary rollout plan and a proposed timeline for the PoC (2–3 sprints -> baseline + regression checks).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Sara Khan <sara@nimbus.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Menon <r.menon@nimbus.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 13:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo action: prioritized model slate + regression guardrails

Jordan — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) When you say ‘confidence < 0.6’ for fallback, is that Redwood’s internal calibrated score or a prompt-specific heuristic? We want to be sure we can reproduce on our side.
2) Can you break the cost table down by payload sizes? Our billing docs show a wide variance between short/long sessions.
3) For the sensitive legal prompts, would you recommend keeping full-fp32 for the PoC (even if costy) to avoid early regressions?

We’re generally aligned on prioritization: legal then billing then support transcripts. Rajesh will coordinate procurement timelines — he’s copied.

— Sara
CTO, Nimbus Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Khan <sara@nimbus.ai>, Rajesh Menon <r.menon@nimbus.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 14:20:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo action: prioritized model slate + regression guardrails

Sara / team — quick technical notes on the three bullets Sara raised: 

1) Confidence score: that was our model-agnostic calibrated logit-based confidence (we provide a small adaptor you can run to match our calibration). We’ll include the adaptor in the repo link. It’s reproducible — thresholding is prompt-aware, so we recommend per-prompt thresholds from a 500-sample validation slice.

2) Cost by payload: attached CSV breaks down cost for 32/128/512 token responses and includes batch amortization assumptions. For interactive UI median case (32 tokens out), RedOpt-13B-8q sits at ~$0.0036 per call; for long-form 512-token flows Falcon-40B-INT8-light is ~ $0.018 per call under dedicated pricing. We’ll annotate the CSV with the assumptions.

3) Sensitive legal prompts: recommendation — run those on full-fp32 Llama2-70B for the initial validation pass (first sprint), but flip them to RedOpt-13B-8q under a hybrid policy once you have 1k validated samples and the sampling checks pass. That minimizes early risk while keeping overall PoC cost reasonable.

Additional asks from Redwood side: 
- Can Nimbus share a 500-sample labeled split for legal/billing (we’ll treat as confidential)? This will let us produce per-prompt threshold candidates and sampling policies.
- Preferred timeline: if we get data by end of next week, Redwood can deliver thresholds + an automated canary plan within 7 business days.


--
Marissa Cole
Director, Model Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: latency_cost_estimates.csv

Thanks all — good alignment. Quick commitments and timeline: 

1) Nimbus: please share the 500-sample labeled legal split (S3 link or secure Drive) by next Friday 2026-12-18. Rajesh, any procurement notes we should expect?
2) Redwood: we’ll push the prompt adapter + confidence calibration script to the shared Drive by Monday 2026-12-14 and run the initial evals. Expect the per-prompt thresholds + canary rollout plan by 2026-12-22.
3) Pilot timeline: 2 sprints (validation + guarded rollout). Canary policy: start with 10% traffic to 8-bit model for non-sensitive prompts; legal prompts remain on fp32 until threshold validated.

Can we lock a 30-min meeting next Tue (2026-12-15) 11:00–11:30 PT to review the thresholding approach? I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Jordan
